year has distinct_count 1 (only 2013.0) and is fully reconstructable from observation_timestamp, so per the operator's single-DATE-column convention it is dropped as a redundant integer part.
month spans only 1.0-6.0 across 6 distinct_values and is derivable from observation_timestamp, so it is dropped as a redundant calendar part per the single-DATE-column convention.
day ranges 1.0-31.0 across 31 distinct values and is derivable from observation_timestamp, so it is dropped as a redundant calendar part per the single-DATE-column convention.
hour ranges 0.0-23.0 across 24 distinct integral values with null_rate 0.0, so DECIMAL(38,9) is safely cast to INTEGER and kept required.
temp samples (e.g. 10.94 to 93.92) all carry two decimal places with null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2) and renamed with its unit suffix per operator convention.
dewp ranges from -9.94 to 73.94 with consistent two-decimal samples and null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2) and renamed with its unit suffix.
humid ranges 12.74 to 100.0 across 2178 distinct two-decimal values with null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2) and renamed with its percent unit suffix.
wind_dir ranges 0.0-360.0 but has null_rate 0.016828 (219 of 13014 nulls), so it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2), renamed with its degrees unit suffix, and retained nullable rather than imputed.

wind_speed ranges 0.0 to 1048.36058 with five-decimal precision samples and a low null_rate of 0.000154 (2 nulls), so it is cast to DECIMAL(10,5), renamed with its mph unit suffix, and retained nullable.

wind_gust ranges 16.11092 to 62.14212 but null_rate is 0.745505 (9702 of 13014 nulls), so it is cast to DECIMAL(10,5), renamed with its mph unit suffix, and retained as a sparsely populated nullable column.
precip ranges 0.0 to 1.06 with two-decimal samples and null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2) and renamed with its inches unit suffix.
pressure ranges 983.8 to 1038.4 with null_rate 0.114953 (1496 of 13014 nulls), so it is cast to DECIMAL(6,2), renamed with its millibars unit suffix, and retained nullable.
visib has 20 enumerated distinct_values from 0.0 to 10.0 and null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to DECIMAL(4,2) and renamed with its miles unit suffix.

time_hour samples are consistently ISO-8601 UTC instants (e.g. 2013-01-01T06:00:00Z) across 4341 distinct values with null_rate 0.0, so it is cast to TIMESTAMP and renamed to reflect it carries the full observation date and hour as a single column.

purpose: This silver table provides cleaned hourly weather observations from the three NYC-area airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) for the January-June 2013 window, sourced from ASOS/IEM observations via the nycflights13 weather dataset, feeding downstream joins with flight records on origin and time.
usage: Consumers should join on origin_code and observation_timestamp, the declared grain keys; before aggregating, handle nulls explicitly in wind_direction_degrees, wind_speed_mph, wind_gust_mph, and sea_level_pressure_millibars since these are retained nullable rather than imputed, and be aware wind_gust_mph is sparsely populated (about 74.6% null).
limitations: year, month, and day were dropped as redundant with observation_timestamp per the single-DATE-column convention; no exact-duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was applied; wind_gust_mph remains heavily null (74.6%) and pressure, wind_dir, and wind_speed retain smaller null rates (11.5%, 1.7%, and 0.015% respectively) that were not imputed or resolved.
